answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel-mechanics declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record has two mutually corroborating findings on exactly that mechanism: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift). Onboarding simplification is upstream of activation, so a single experiment plausibly moves both declining metrics, which matters when the slot does not carry over. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records strong acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention drop and an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, buying accounts that churn in 30 days is the wrong trade, and matching a competitor on price is the direction hardest to reverse once it anchors customer expectations. Referral incentive (memory_57) is credible but scoped to established customers and does not address the funnel declines; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a segment that is not the one under attack; activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strongest fallback and is my second choice, but it nudges behavior downstream of the friction rather than removing it. I am spending verification on the two memories I am actually acting on rather than on the one I am declining, since memory_73's caveat is already recorded and re-reading it changes nothing. What I want from the archive: whether memory_86's lift was measured on completion and adoption only or followed through to retention and qualified revenue, and whether memory_31's 'durable' claim rests on a horizon longer than a few weeks. Key risk to flag: both source findings are proxy metrics (completion, first-week activation) that were consolidated as wins without confirmed revenue attachment, and stripping signup fields can degrade lead qualification data, which would quietly convert a funnel win into a pipeline-quality loss. Also note memory_31 and memory_86 may be partly the same effect counted twice rather than independent confirmation. So: standard experiment with retention, lead-quality, and qualified-revenue instrumentation alongside completion, not a broad rollout. If verification shows the original lifts never touched revenue or decayed after week one, I switch to activation_messaging.
